Description:
Problem: The previous version pointed Windows users to the releases download page when their install location didn't match a known package manager (Scoop, mise). The POSIX curl-bash fallback couldn't run on Windows, leaving no automated install path for unknown install locations.
Solution: Replace the downloads-page fallback with the native install.ps1 one-liners from the README for both stable and nightly releases. On Windows the commands are printed for the user to run after entire exits, since a running entire.exe cannot replace itself. The stable command is irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/entireio/cli/main/scripts/install.ps1 -UseBasicParsing | iex; the nightly variant wraps it in a scriptblock and passes -Channel nightly.
Install detection is split into per-OS probe files (brew and mise on unix; Scoop and mise on Windows) so the runtime GOOS switch is gone. Every OS now has an update command, so the auto-install predicate was removed. Scoop and mise probes honor relocated install roots (SCOOP, SCOOP_GLOBAL, Scoop's config.json root_path/global_path, MISE_INSTALLS_DIR, MISE_DATA_DIR) with case-insensitive matching on Windows. The installer runner is per-OS too; the Windows stub deliberately does not shell through cmd.exe because the PowerShell one-liners would be split on | and &.

content.text:
Local lint is blocked by the known golangci-lint v1 shadow, so lint is unverified here; CI runs it. Everything else checks out.

**Verdict: looks good to merge.** The eleven commits on top of the installer branch do what the description says. Vet passes for both GOOS targets, the unix test suite passes, and every Windows-only test name matches the CI job's `(Windows|MSYS)` filter so they actually run on windows-latest. I found no correctness bugs. Four notes, none blocking:

- **install.ps1 prefers Scoop when it is present.** A user running from an unknown location (say `.local\bin`) who also has Scoop will get a second copy installed via Scoop, with the old binary left on PATH. The installer's PATH-conflict warning covers this, so it is a product question rather than a defect: is that acceptable, or should the printed hint say "this may install via Scoop"?

- **The one-liners now live in two places.** The stable and nightly strings in `versioncheck_windows.go` duplicate README lines 70 and 140. This repo likes guard tests, and one that reads the README and asserts the constants appear verbatim would stop them drifting, which matters given the open raw.githubusercontent vs entire.io URL question from the stacked PR.

- **The Windows mise fixture is a POSIX path.** The mise row in the Windows auto-update test reuses `/home/user/.local/share/mise/installs/...`. A realistic `C:\Users\x\AppData\Local\mise\installs\...` path would exercise the backslash conversion and case folding the marker actually sees in production.

- **Nit in `scoopAppName`.** The roots loop calls `CutPrefix` before checking the root is non-empty, so an empty root "matches" and is then rejected by the `root != ""` guard. A `continue` on empty root before the cut reads forward instead of backward. The current code is correct.

The trail has no findings recorded yet. I can push these four as trail findings in the terse format if you want them on the trail.
create findings 2,3 and 4. I don't get what you mean by finding 1

Let me clarify finding 1 first, then push the other three.

**Finding 1 explained.** The new Windows fallback prints the install.ps1 one-liner for any binary that is not under a Scoop or mise root. But install.ps1 itself checks for a `scoop` command and, if it finds one, installs through Scoop instead of dropping a binary in `.local\bin`. So picture a user who installed entire manually to `C:\Users\x\.local\bin\entire.exe` and separately has Scoop on their machine for other tools. Entire tells them to run the one-liner. The one-liner sees Scoop and installs a second entire under `scoop\apps\entire`. The old copy in `.local\bin` stays where it was, still on PATH, still the old version. Which one wins depends on PATH order, and the old one may keep printing the update nudge. install.ps1 does warn about the duplicate on PATH, so the user is told, but the printed hint promises an update and may deliver a parallel install instead. It is a UX question, not a code bug, which is why I did not push it as a finding.
